expectations.description: Does NOT simply validate the Fornell-Larcker criterion as sufficient evidence for discriminant validity without raising concerns about its limitations
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states 'The Fornell-Larcker criterion has poor sensitivity — it routinely fails to flag discriminant validity problems' and frames FL as 'a necessary but insufficient condition,' directly raising concerns about its limitations rather than validating it as sufficient evidence.

expectations.description: States that the Fornell-Larcker criterion has low sensitivity — it frequently fails to detect discriminant validity violations that exist
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'Henseler, Ringle, & Sarstedt (2015, JAMS) demonstrated via simulation that the FL criterion has poor sensitivity — it routinely fails to flag discriminant validity problems, especially when factor correlations are moderate-to-high.'

expectations.description: Names the HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio of correlations) as the current standard for assessing discriminant validity in CFA/SEM contexts
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly names HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio) as 'the current best-practice criterion' and states in the summary table that it is 'now the standard', citing Henseler et al. (2015) as the source.

expectations.description: States the HTMT threshold: values below .85 provide evidence of discriminant validity for conceptually distinct constructs (or .90 for closely related constructs)
expectations.evidence: The response states: 'HTMT < .85 (strict; conceptually distinct constructs)' and 'HTMT < .90 (liberal; conceptually related constructs)'

expectations.description: Recommends computing HTMT — e.g., via semTools::htmt() in R — rather than relying solely on Fornell-Larcker
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly recommends computing HTMT and provides code: 'library(semTools)\nhtmt(model, data = yourdata)' — directly recommending semTools::htmt() in R rather than relying solely on Fornell-Larcker, which it critiques as 'necessary but insufficient.'

expectations.description: Clarifies that AVE > .50 is a criterion for convergent validity (each construct explains more than half the variance in its indicators), not for discriminant validity — the two criteria serve different purposes
expectations.evidence: The model response never clarifies that AVE > .50 is a criterion for convergent validity (explaining more than half the variance in indicators), not discriminant validity. It treats AVE solely in the context of the Fornell-Larcker discriminant validity criterion without distinguishing that AVE > .50 serves a separate purpose as a convergent validity benchmark.
